prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a downward-angled outdoor scene on a sloped brick sidewalk beside a street, showing the ground plane receding from roughly 0.5–1.5 m at the bottom edge to dark >3 m road background at the top. In frame 1, a person in a black jacket on the lower right (holding a phone) is bright white at ~0.6–0.9 m (within the camera wearer's arm's reach), a person in an olive jacket on the left is at ~1.2–1.5 m partially occluding a person in blue behind them at ~1.8–2.2 m, and two standing figures in grey and dark clothing near the top center/right are farther away at ~2.0–2.8 m and spaced ~0.8–1.0 m apart. As the camera wearer turns their head leftward in frames 2–3 and then back to the right in frames 4–5, a woman in black holding a phone on the far left (with a flat menu sign behind her) enters at ~0.5–0.8 m in frames 2–4 before moving out of view as the person in the black jacket on the right returns to ~0.7–1.0 m in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes from the similarly toned brick steps and orders overlapping people in depth (such as the olive-jacketed person in front of the blue-jacketed person and the menu board behind the woman on the left). However, the map is unreliable on the flat printed graphics of the sign in frames 2–3 (rendering parts of the 2D surface at inconsistent depths) and merges the lower legs of the more distant standing people into the surrounding sidewalk gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels individual people and small objects across the sidewalk cluster, distinguishing up to six person instances along with a cell phone, a car, a handbag, and a backpack. In frame 1, it separates the close person on the lower right (~0.6–0.9 m, partially cut off at the frame edge) and the phone in their hands from the person in the olive jacket on the left (~1.2–1.5 m), the partially occluded person in blue behind them (~1.8 m), and two standing people further up the sidewalk (~2.0–2.8 m, about 1 m apart). As the viewpoint pans left in frames 2–3, it segments the close woman in black on the left (~0.5–0.8 m, facing right and looking down at a segmented cell phone within her own and the camera wearer's arm's reach) and a white car in the upper-right street (>3.5 m away), then tracks the pan back right in frames 4–5 to reveal two additional distant people in the upper right (~2.5–3.5 m). This map makes small held or worn objects (the phones in frames 1, 3, and 4, and the shoulder strap/bags in frames 3–4) and heavily occluded background pedestrians immediately distinct from the busy RGB background. However, it is unreliable in several places: it splits single individuals into multiple overlapping 'person' masks (the olive-jacketed person in frame 1 and the grey-hoodie person in frames 1 and 3), mislabels the occluded person in blue as a 'backpack' in frame 4, and misses the phones in frames 2 and 5 as well as the menu board entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates body skeletons (yellow) and hand skeletons (magenta) on a black background, showing torso orientation, limb articulation, and hand configurations where detected. It captures the body skeleton of only one distant person per frame—the person in blue on the upper left in frame 1 (~1.8–2.2 m away, angled toward the right), the person in the grey hoodie in frame 2 (~2.2–2.5 m away, facing the camera wearer with hands in pockets), and the person with long hair in frame 5 (~2.0–2.3 m away, facing the camera wearer with arms crossed)—while detecting isolated 3D hand skeletons at ~0.6–0.9 m in the foreground (the right-side person's two hands holding a phone in frame 1, and the left-side woman's phone-holding hands in frames 2–4). These keypoints make precise finger curl, wrist orientation, and the frontal body alignment of the distant standing figures easier to read than in the wide-angle, fish-eye distorted RGB frames. Across the 5-frame head pan from right to left and back, the foreground magenta hand skeletons shift across the lower field of view within ~0.5–0.9 m (arm's reach of both their owners and the camera wearer) before disappearing in frame 5 when the close right-side person's hands are tucked away. However, the pose map is highly sparse and unreliable for full-scene understanding, completely missing the body skeletons of all foreground and mid-ground people (including the olive-jacketed person, the close woman on the left, and the close man on the right) and failing to detect any head keypoints for the people looking toward or away from the camera wearer.
